annotations.text:
The record, rebuilt from ADR-0020

This page is the system: the anatomy every surface inherits and the tokens every surface is drawn from. The Surfaces page applies it thirteen times; the Variants page is the light theme and the longest-language check.

The artboards are generated. gen.py builds every one from a single skeleton, so a change to the anatomy is one edit rather than thirteen, and two screens cannot drift apart by hand. gen.py --light regenerates the light variant from the same code with only the token values swapped, which is the claim tokens.css makes and this is the proof of it.

Copy comes from src/locales/. A string here that is not in the catalogue is the artboard inventing interface.

The tokens had a guard and never a meaning

A file of hex values does not say that surface-terminal is deepest because that is where the eye rests, or that warn belongs to connecting and to armed broadcast and to nothing else.

The red box is the honest part. The guard is strong and there is one thing it cannot see.

Every screen a person can meet, in the anatomy ADR-0020 fixed

Each rectangle in the main area is a group: a 28px strip of tabs plus the body of the active one. A surface belonging to a session renders in the group whose active tab it is, which is why the host key screens and the failure screen sit inside one rectangle while the terminals around them keep running.

A credential window used to be the exception, a separate OS window under ADR-0008 so a document rendering hostile terminal output was never the document holding a password. ADR-0039 retired it: every credential is now collected inline, in a group like everything else here, and no artboard on this page draws a window of its own any more.

The safety markers, in one place

Armed broadcast reaches the active tab of each group, so a session behind another is connected and not receiving. Four markers say what is happening and none of them is colour alone: a checked square on each receiving tab, a warn border around each receiving group, a check in the sidebar row with SPARED on the ones held out, and the whole top edge of the status bar turning warn with the count and the way off.

The rail is pinned and locked while armed. The sidebar may still be closed: every receiving host has a tab naming it.

The two screens that are the product's argument

Unknown key: the primary button is inert until the out-of-band checkbox is ticked, because clicking through is the failure the screen exists to prevent.

Changed key: the safe action is the only filled button, the override is low contrast and dead until the host name is typed. A rebuilt host and a machine in the middle look identical from here, and only one of them is survivable.

The randomart is drawn because it exists on feat/visual-improvements. Its test pins the implementation's own output rather than ssh-keygen -lv, which is tracked in #135.

Light, and the longest-language check

MainLight is generated by gen.py --light: the same code, the same layout, only the token values swapped. If light ever needed a different layout, tokens.css would be making a claim it could not keep.

MainPtBr and MainEs come from gen-locales.mjs, which substitutes catalogue strings into the English artboard and fails hard when a replacement does not match exactly once. Terminal output stays English on purpose: remote text is never translated.

What is not here yet: locale variants of the host key screens. The old canvas had them and that is where its one real layout break was found, so they are worth rebuilding rather than quietly dropped.
